name: Brali outcome observation policy

north_star.definition: Unique protocol runs with both a protocol_completed event and an explicit helpful_yes event in the same ISO week, using the same run_id and a published Brali dataset version.
north_star.observed_value_must_come_from: Reviewed, explicit opt-in outcome events listed in data/outcome-observations.json. Demo, fixture, CI, page-view, repository and generated events never count.

opt_in_channels.description: The browser prepares a privacy-light event in a prefilled GitHub issue. The user reviews and submits it explicitly. Raw query text is omitted.
The browser shares the event JSON through the operating system share sheet. No destination is selected by Brali.
The browser downloads the event JSON locally for manual review or later submission. Downloading is not collection.
A maintainer may add a reviewed, consented event to data/outcome-observations.json with provenance and verification metadata.

privacy_contract.prompt_text_may_be_shared_separately: Only when the user deliberately adds it after reviewing the destination. It is never part of the outcome event envelope.
minimum_context: canonical Topic and Protocol identifiers where available

retention.browser: Event previews exist only in page memory unless the user shares or downloads them.
retention.github_issue: Submitted issue content follows GitHub and repository retention controls. Users can edit or delete their issue subject to platform permissions.
retention.public_observation_dataset: Only reviewed events with explicit consent and no personal data may be copied into the versioned public observation dataset.
retention.aggregate_report: Aggregate reports contain counts and canonical IDs, not raw prompts or user identifiers.

verification.verified_success_rule: Count a run only when protocol_completed and helpful_yes are both present, valid and linked by the same run_id.

reporting_rules: Show zero when no reviewed observations exist.
Separate observed counts from hypotheses, targets, demos and fixtures.
Do not infer users, completions or helpfulness from page views, copies, downloads, repository activity or CI.
Publish failed, not-helpful, bad-match and no-answer outcomes when they meet the same consent and privacy boundary.
Do not claim repeated use without repeated reviewed observations from a privacy-safe integration identifier or explicitly linked run series.
